== Walkthrough ==


=== Scoundrel's Hovel ===
Upon entering the dungeon you will need to swim through a tunnel with mines. The mines will do significant damage and cripple you, so don't get close. Once on the other side, players will reach Inspector Kiel. Players will take the lead and go around the corner to take out the group of Aetherblade. Go through the doorway and take out the next group to reach the electric walls.


=== Electrified Catwalks ===
This is the first new mechanic to learn. Players can walk over electrical plates, but it will do a very large amount of damage, usually downing you before you finish passing through it. The plates turn off and on, allowing you to step through (for slower GPUs, "dodge forward" works well). Inspector Kiel will wait behind while you figure out how to turn them off. Wait until a plate is off and pass through each one in turn until you reach the far side. Inside the hut there are three switches. Activate each one to turn off all electrical plates and Inspector Kiel will catch up with you. Continue through the passageways, avoiding other electrical plates, and turning them off when possible.


=== Breach the Gate ===
After the walls, you'll reach an area where you need to get past a gate. Several waves of Aetherblade will attack you. This is also where the next mechanic is learned. While fighting, an Aetherblade Cannoneer will be on a ledge firing cannons at the players, creating fire AoE fields on the ground wherever they hit. As the fight goes on, a second cannoneer on the other side will do the same thing. These cannoneers are invulnerable, so defeat all of the gate guards to open it. After a short run you'll reach the gate to Frizz's Lab for the mid-boss fight.


=== Frizz's Lab ===
Talk to Inspector Kiel to begin the boss fight. A cinematic will play showing the area. You'll have a chance to see the area and make plans. Talk to Frizz to trigger the event. Frizz will run around with a Flamethrower while you fight him and his assistants. Once you bring him down to 75% health, he jumps to the center and enters a protective tube. Two walls of electricity, similar to the electric walls encountered earlier, will emerge from opposite sides of the center tube and slowly rotate counter-clockwise. The walls will do a significant amount of damage if it hits you. Players can either move along with the walls, climb up on the stacks of crates and barrels spread across the room, or even jump over the electric walls if they time it right (this is very difficult, but possible). Teleport skills will safely transport players through them.
You will not be able to damage Frizz during this time, but he will send two golems at a time to fight you. These golems will be supercharged if the walls pass over them, giving them a damage boost, so avoid being hit while it's in effect. Either kite the golems or soak up their damage. Ranged attacks are best during this fight, although mainly due to mobility since the golems have some ranged attacks too. When supercharged, they can also use a pull skill to bring you close to them.
Once 2 golems have been defeated, Frizz will increase the power, doubling the size of the walls, and send two more golems after you. Players will not be able to avoid these walls by standing on the crates or jumping over, so move counter-clockwise around the room while attacking the golems and try to keep them from being supercharged by the walls.
Once those two golems are defeated, he then activates both the tall and short electric walls at once. The smaller wall is just like the first wall but travels faster than the taller one. Two more golems will fight you during this time. Players will need to again move counter-clockwise to avoid the taller wall, but also jump onto the crates to avoid the smaller one as it will travel faster than you.
Once the third set of golems are destroyed, the fight ends and players can continue.


=== The Wretched Walk ===
After the fight, continue traveling north along the passageway and it will curve south. A storm is picking up, and the rope bridges will get struck by lightning often. Avoid the lightning and cross the bridges to reach the other side. In the middle of the bridge section there will be several Aetherblades. This section is a death trap, as the Aetherblades are powerful and you don't have much room to maneuver. Take them out and continue along the bridges.
There will be an Aetherblade Cache along the way and you will reach the third waypoint.


=== Deceit's Climb ===
Continue to travel through the tunnels. Inspector Kiel will wait at some closed doors while players work to open them. Travel up and defeat the veterans and pirates waiting there to open it up. Continue on to the docks.


=== Aethership Dock ===
Talk to Inspector Kiel to enter the boss fight area. After a short cinematic, Mai Trin and Horrik will attack you. Mai has a buff called Captain's Shield, which reduces damage done to her by 10% per stack. She begins with 10 stacks and she must be hit by Horrik's electric fields to remove them. She also shadowsteps around and uses electric attacks and bleeds. Horrik will stand off to the side and fire cannonballs and electric shots at players, creating burning and electric fields. Lure Mai into the electric fields to reduce the Captain's Shield and take her out.
If players focus on Horrik instead and kill him first, Mai will revive him, creating a shockwave (similar to the Molten Berserker from Molten Facility). Reviving Horrik also seems to reset her Captain's Shield. Horrik should be ignored until Mai is down or nearly down. In the last phase of killing Mai, it is reasonable to hit Horrik also so that he is less of a problem when Mai is downed. Mai seems to have several noticeable tactics. She notices who is reviving and attacks them, she targets the character furthest away from her, and probably other tactics that others might add.
Once Mai reaches 75%, she and Horrik teleport away and two cannoneers appear, raining fire down on the players similar to the gate section earlier. The pattern of shots are different each volley, so stay on the move. After about 45 seconds of this, Mai and Horrik appear to continue the fight. This cannon interludes happens again at 50% and 25%, each time adding more cannons (which means more fields) and the volleys happen more often, and the duration is longer also. The first time the cannons lasts for 60 seconds, then 80, and finally 120 on the last phase. Note that the volleys target players, so having multiple players stack up in the same place is not advised, as it will create multiple overlapping fields with no safe place to stand in between. Instead, spread out and simply sidestep the AOEs when they appear. Stealth can also be used to briefly prevent cannoneers from targeting you, but it will not negate any projectiles already en route.
One alternative tactic often used by players is to designate a run leader and stack up moments before the barrage phase (E.G. ~80% or so health on the first barrage and so on). When the barrage phase occurs, the players will follow the run leader closely and run as a group clockwise or counterclockwise around the edges of the room. This method is recommended if the party has a substantial amount of regen/swiftness, as it reduces the pressure on individual players substantially. Downed teammates can be tended to after the barrage phase.
Once Mai is defeated, Horrik becomes frenzied and now you must finish him.


=== Destroy the escaping Aethership ===
Once Horrik is down, he drops a Cannon Core. If the battle was won in less than 15 minutes, players have a chance to destroy the escaping Aethership. Use the new red platforms to move over to the waiting airship and use the core on the cannon up front to destroy the airship.

== Getting there ==

== Mechanics ==


=== Crystals ===
Small blue crystals refill 10% of the player's endurance, allowing them to use Light Dash more often. Orange crystal grant 3 seconds of swiftness and vigor. The aspect crystals provide one charge of the augmented aspect skill, which means doubling the height of Leap and the range for Light Dash and Lightning Pull. Using the augmented variants of skills does not affect the cooldown of the standard skill nor does the augmented Light Dash consume endurance.


=== Power ups ===
There are two types of power ups: defensive and offensive. Players will receive Aspect Master or Grounded from defensive power ups and Fake Power-Up, Gale, Lightning Rod, or Blinding Light from offensive power ups. Players in first place will only receive Fake Power-Up and Grounded. Players in the farthest half of the racers can receive Light Travel from defensive upgrades and the stronger versions of Gale, Lightning Rod, or Blinding Light from offensive power ups.

== Mechanics ==
Players are separated into two teams placed on opposite sides. Each side has three elemental crystals representing the three aspects: wind, sun, and lightning. The aspect crystals grant five distinct abilities associated with their element. Within the arena, there are six spawn points for attunement crystals, two of which will be active at any given time. If a player can take a crystal back to the aspect crystals within their base, their team gains 50 points. Player kills count for 1 point. The team with the most points when the timer runs out wins. Players who are carrying a crystal are under the effect of Aspect Crystal.
All players are limited to 100 health and have all healing, utility, and elite skills locked. Thus the only skills available during the event are the aspect skills.


== Skills ==
The movement skills in slot 5 use up endurance. Assisted Leap and Lightning Tether uses 50 points. Speed of Light uses 40 points.

== Mechanics ==
This is a PvP activity in which players attempt to be the last survivor. Players' skills are limited to the items that they are able to find throughout the map. Each skill has limited uses so players must determine the best time to use each.
Players begin the match  Immobile, circling a stockpile of resources and weapons. Once the announcement ends, players are free to grab whatever they can and are allowed to attack each other. At the beginning of each match, there is a Grace Period that prevents players from being removed too early in the game.


=== Survivors ===
 Hungry — You're losing health to hunger.
Survivors suffer from the hunger effect, slowly reducing the player's health over time and increasing in intensity as the match progresses. To survive from this effect, players must find and consume rations which recover their health but not reset the stack of hunger. Survivors can gather arrows for their bow attacks, traps, or other bundle weapons. Killing other players does not allow you to loot the items they were holding. Pickpocket Trap can however.


==== Survivor weapon skills ====
Each weapon listed below has a durability or ammunition count. Ammunition is consumed after use of a skill and durability is consumed after hitting a foe with a skill. When the number reaches zero, the weapon will be replaced with the default bow.


==== Survivor utility skills ====

After a survivor dies or if a player enters after the grace period ends, they become a mist walker.


=== Mist Walkers ===
 Mist Walker — You've faded into the Mists. Collect revenge motes to power skills that hinder living competitors.
Mist walkers gather Revenge Motes to harass the remaining survivors. Revenge motes appear throughout the map and at the location of a survivor whenever attempt to gather anything.

== Walkthrough ==
At the start of the match, if possible, grab the Pistol immediately, and keep it with you at all times. Save the shots and only use it if a player is intent on killing you. This weapon can be considered overpowered as it almost instantly kills any player within range and it has 2 charges.
If another player grabs a pistol, grab an arrow immediately use   Head Shot to kill off the other player, note that you will have a 2 and 3/4 seconds of charge time before your arrow is shot.
Once the match starts, keep pressure on the player with the pistol to use it, as the first 3 minutes you would respawn if you were to die.
You don't need to kill other players unless they are a danger to you or would otherwise outlast you, since points don't matter; the last survivor is the winner.
When the match begins, focus on finding as many Passifloras to gain Rations (be wary of suspiciously placed Passifloras which might be traps placed by other players). You can stock up to 10 charges of Rations.
Stay in an open area where you cannot get surrounded by Karkas summoned by Mist Walkers (dead players). Keep looking around you and Sprint away fast if someone spawns a Karka. If you are near the sea, you can jump into it too (provided it has no sharks or other hostile creatures), since Karkas cannot swim.
The safest and easiest way to win is to just hide somewhere far from camps and let the other players kill themselves, and wait for them to run out of Rations while you're fully stocked up. Use a Ration every time you tick down to around 300 health left (just in case you're attacked by a Mist Walker).
When there are only a few survivors left, and if you have a Pistol, this is the time to use it. Shoot anyone you see, as they'll probably try to kill you.
Placing a trap directly on top of another player will not trigger it immediately. Try to lay the trap in front of where they are moving for immediate results.

The Crown Pavilion within Divinity's Reach proper is the upper level of the Crown Pavilion arena that is located within the huge sinkhole that was once known as the Great Collapse. The Crown Pavilion is a large arena built to commemorate humanity's resilience despite their hardships, and the renovation of the district was the Queen's Jubilee that marked Queen Jennah's 10th year as queen of Kryta. The plans for these renovations were in place for a few years.
There are portals to access the middle levels of the Crown Pavilion (which are within the area, not the zone).


== History ==
The Canthan and Arts District in Divinity's Reach was established since the founding of the city in 1220 AE and had several Canthan immigrants moving in after access to Cantha had been cut off by the rising of Orr and the spreading influence of the Elder Dragon Zhaitan. As it grew, the district had theatres, craftsmen, and entertainment, including the Great Symphony Hall. It collapsed sometime between 1324 and early 1325 AE due to a rushed construction and being placed atop a cavernous sinkhole which local Krytans had used as tombs in the past. Some of the residents who had escaped the collapse migrated to neighboring districts.
There are conflicting stories on what happened the night of the collapse. According to the Shining Blade the sewer system had collapsed and there had been warning signs a couple weeks before the disaster. Accordingly, they took steps to work with the Seraph to evacuate all residents from the district. Some citizens reported the collapse happening in multiple stages with cracks appearing first, and a main collapse happening later. However, many locals never mentioned that the Seraph were involved with protecting the citizens, and along with this, Riot Alice said that her father had died during the collapse. There were also rumors of strange noises coming from the depths of the Great Collapse, which were associated with pre-existing rumors of stories of drakes living in the city's sewer system.
In 1326 AE, the district was rebuilt as the Crown Pavilion, an arena for duels and mass brawls which both commemorated humanity's resilience and celebrated Queen Jennah's tenth year as the monarch of Kryta. The festivities were interrupted by two surprise attacks led by the sylvari terrorist Scarlet Briar who set off several bombs which claimed many lives, activated tampered watchknights to attack surviving citizens and soldiers, and attempted to kidnap the queen. Although Scarlet was ultimately driven off, the aftermath of the attack led to the watchknights being pulled back until they were reprogrammed and reinstated for the Siege of Divinity's Reach in 1330 AE with an official public return to the Crown Pavilion for the Festival of the Four Winds in 1331 AE.

== Trivia ==
At one point during development, this area was originally a completed Canthan district and included a blend of Asian architectures. Shortly before release, developers were told to remove it, and no official reason has ever been given. Due to time constraints the district was replaced by the Great Collapse. However, there have also been developer comments stating that the originally planned existence of the Canthan district should not be considered canonical.
Both "crown" and "pavilion" are terms used in diamond cutting, and the shape of the area itself may be meant to resemble a brilliant cut diamond with the pavilion leveled off and the elaborate glass-winged eagle representing the crown.

== Walkthrough ==
Your next stop is the spire at Skimshallow Cove. Don't be misled by the sand portal at the base of the spire. Ignore it and use a Springer to climb to the platform (about halfway up) then walk up the steps and the plank. Enter the story instance and you're suddenly thrust into single combat with Balthazar himself.
Balthazar isn't very mobile, using only leap attacks to move about or slowly walking towards you. But he attacks with flaming AoE attacks covering most of the arena. Ultimately, he's only toying with you: if you go down, he'll revive you himself. At every 20% health, he'll become invincible and gain new skills; at 60% and 20% health he will down you and cause you to be Wounded and then Deeply Wounded. You will automatically rally, but become increasingly injured. As soon as his health reaches 10%, he tires of his game - and kills you.
You awaken in ghostly form in a strange environment. Move northeast to have a chat with an imprisoned Palawa Joko, then follow Nenah to The Judge. Search the crates in the center area near Brapp until you retrieve your weapons and abilities. Pursue the spirits with your name and destroy them, which should be easy. Additionally, if you are in a party, your party members will have three skills available to them by default;

Follow the bird named "Your Purpose" as it summons scenes from your previous adventures from the tutorial to when Balthazar defeated you, bringing your memories back. Return to the Judge and jog off to kill this area's boss, the Eater of Souls. His most difficult mechanic is a ranged and AoE self-heal that he can use to drain life from you. Here's some advice to deal with it:

The health drain attack is deadly while close but does lower damage and healing while far away, so keep your distance.
The drain can be interrupted by fast and well-timed crowd control skills. Keep a few of them ready. If you break him during this moment, he becomes vulnerable for long enough that you can deal heavy damage to him. The defiance bar doesn't last long, so control skills must have very fast activation times of less than half a second, have instant activation if possible. If you bring extra party members, they can use Eerie Whisper to assist.
The Eater will use a leap attack just before using the drain. If fighting at range he'll leap at you and while fighting from melee-range he will basically leap in place.
Focus on dealing damage rather than defending. The fight is a contest between your damage output and his ability to heal off you.
Use pets or minions as he will not regain health from them if he does his drain.
Return to gloat about your victory to Palawa Joko, then open the indicated portal back to Tyria. After some banter with your excited guildmates, the mission ends.

== Notes ==

The difficulty of the Eater of Souls fight was reduced in a October 5, 2017 patch: "Drastically decreased the amount of health the Eater of Souls can steal. Increased the duration the defiance bar is vulnerable on the Eater of Souls's leap attack. Removed the Eater of Souls's ability to steal health from pets and minions."
While in Judgment, the following notes apply:
Party members will accompany the instance owner as wisp-like "spirit guardians". They will have a minor buff, a vulnerable attack skill and a regeneration skill instead of their usual abilities.
Lost spirits have no pockets: no access to inventory while dead. Therefore, combat consumables should be used before getting killed by Balthazar.
It's still possible to change equipped weapon to another in inventory via the Hero Panel's Equipment page.
Ghosts are weightless: they take no fall damage. However, party members' spirit guardians are not weightless, and will take fall damage.
Mounts and gliders cannot be used.
Until the spirit of the commander finds a weapon, the bottom part of the user interface is hidden. Once it reappears, the health bowl will be blue instead of red.
Until they reclaim their name, the mini map stays hidden.
Until they reclaim their name, their name in chat, over character, and in hero panel is changed to "Lost Spirit".

== My story ==


== Notes ==
This story step, unlocked at level 40, takes place lore-wise before the events of the story mode of Ascalonian Catacombs, which is unlocked at level 30.
This story step was originally part of the first order-specific story steps as its own instance. It was separated post-release development to put the identical meeting from the three starting missions of the different Orders into one instance 
Like all other Personal Story chapters, this story step takes place in 1325 AE, in an older version of Lion's Arch. The Lion's Arch that players see before entering the instance is the modern appearance of the area after the rebuilding following the outcome of Living World Season 1.
The old version of Lion's Arch get coloured with a sepia tone added with post-processing which can be disabled by selecting Postprocessing: None in the Graphics Options (F11).
With the re-release of Living World Season 1, the old version of Lion's Arch can be fully visited again at any time by using of the Lion's Pride Gizmo, earned by completing the Lion's Memory achievement.
Before the rebuilding of Lion's Arch, players doing this story step would come across a group of children playing pretend as Destiny's Edge. With the rebuilding of Lion's Arch, this instance suffered some minor changes, most notable these children were relocated from the main ramp leading into the instance to an easily-missable area to the right of the ramp the character is coming from (northwest of the fountain). As a result, nowadays most players do not notice them and skip their dialogue which summarises the lore of Destiny's Edge.

== Walkthrough ==
First you have a drinking contest. There are three rounds. The goal is to reduce your enemy's HP to zero before you die.

Drink competition skills

Skill 1 reduces both of your HP.
Skill 2 causes your next drink to not reduce your HP, but might cause the enemy to release poison.
Skill 3 heals both you and the enemy.
Skill 4 is channeled appears to add hidden effects, but only works some of the time.
It may cause your Drink Water to heal 100% more.
It may cause your Drink Water to heal 200% more and cause regeneration for 6 seconds.
It may damage your opponent.
It may make the audience ignore your next Fakeout.
It may make your next Belch stronger.
Skill 5 is only available for a few seconds after using #1, allows you to poison the enemy, and it's stronger when your HP is low. While this skill is not available it will not appear in the skill bar, but its recharge will progress normally.
Exact conditions to make skill 4 work are unclear but seem to be related to how much more HP you have over your enemy, and/or how many drinks you have had without drinking water, and/or if the enemy is poisoned from Skill 5.
General strategy is to alternate between 1 and 2, then release 5 when your HP is low, then boast with skill 4, then recover using 3. Sometimes the poison released from 2 hurts more than drinking, in that case just don't use 2.
For the final pirate, use 1 until you're around 200-300 health, and then belch. Sometimes, the belch will knock the opponent to the ground and you can drink water (3) and they will not drink water after you. Use this method to get kill them off. If they do not fall down after you belch, boast, take one drink of water, and then repeat (drink until you're around 200-300 health) until they fall down and you can drink water and they can't. When they stand up, finish them off.
However, the final enemy gets less benefit from healing (she has more health than you, but heals the same amount or less when she drinks water, so healing is less useful for her) a good alternate strategy is to use 1 until you are low on health, then use 5, and then 3. you will gain more benefit (relatively) so you can repeat until they fall.
A safe but much slower strategy is using #1 followed by #5, then using #4 2 times to make time for #5 to recharge, then repeat.
It is possible to get an extra advantage by using food that heals health every second (e.g. Bowl of Candy Corn Custard, Apple Tart, Shiverpeak Ration).

Companion skills during the drink competition [verification requested]

After the contest is over, you will swim to the next island over, where Demmi Beetlestone is being held. Defeat the prison guard; afterwards, a number of other pirates will approach and engage. When they are all defeated, Tybalt will tell you to meet him and Demmi at Whispers HQ in Lion's Arch. Leave the mission instance and travel to Lion's Arch.
The HQ is south of Commodore's Quarter Waypoint. Talk to Bouncer Kinna, then enter the pub instance and go downstairs. Watch the cutscene with Lady Wi, Tybalt, and your other allies. You must then choose which mission you will do next, either They Went Thataway or Thrown Off Guard.

== Walkthrough ==
This mission is fairly short and can avoid combat completely. You will start in the Crow's Nest Tavern and after the initial cutscene you'll be granted invisibility.
Knock out each Ministry Guard as you pass them by standing behind them and pressing the interact button (F by default) when prompted. You will be able to attack them with profession skills (weapon and utility skills being locked from the invisibility), but this is more a hindrance.
Once you reach the middle of the bridge heading towards Grand Piazza, your invisibility will run out and you will now have to avoid being seen. The Grand Piazza is being patrolled by four Ministry Guards, navigate safely through the piazza (Tybalt and Demmi will follow you closely) onto the bridge that leads to Fort Marriner and you are done. Alternatively you can kill all the guards, not terribly difficult as Tybalt and Demmi will assist you.

== Walkthrough ==
You will meet up with a number of other Order of Whispers operatives in the central plaza of Lion's Arch. While Claw Island has been lost, the Risen have not fully infiltrated the city yet, so there is still some time to keep them at bay while the evacuation of the citizens is taking place. The first cinematic brings you up to speed - skipping it will likely bug the mission out later, so it is recommended not to skip it. Your character then volunteers to patrol the Canal Ward. Go to each of the quest markers on the map; there will be NPCs at each one, who will run away after some Risen spawn nearby. Once you have gone to each location and secured it (such that the map marker disappears), head back to the central plaza, and the mission is over. Note that the location with the three children actually has two separate groups of Risen - one at where the children are, and one just to the north.
Risen Plague Carriers explode for massive AoE damage and cause several conditions. Skills that summon extra allies can be very helpful - while Trahearne joins you on this mission, he tends to hang back and use ranged attacks, so the Plague Carriers will tend to target you first.

== Walkthrough ==
Meet back at the Order Headquarter's in Bloodtide Coast. After a brief cutscene you will be promoted to Lightbringer and charged with finding the whereabouts of Yeng Isen, a supposed traitor to the Order.
Head to Lion's Arch and meet up with Tybalt at Yeng's house. After searching the upstairs and concluding that Yeng has been here recently, Tybalt calls your attention to the basement, where there is a tunnel blocked off by some rocks. Clearing them, you find a long, winding passage underground, which is apparently the place Yeng used to house his animals. Many of them are still around, and some have become hostile due to neglect. Kill them on your way to the quest objective. Once you reach the final chamber, Yeng's body is in the middle of the room, and interacting with it (examine) will trigger a short cutscene, after which you will fight his killer - a Risen Creature. After slaying it, the mission ends, and Tybalt will explain that this sort of creature acts as a scout for Zhaitan - Lion's Arch is in imminent danger of invasion.
Notes:

If the "examine" interaction button doesn't appear when standing over Yeng's corpse, it might mean that you have failed to kill all of the escaped creatures on the way.
Rangers will have the opportunity to tame a Juvenile Pink Moa in Yeng's basement.

Enter the house. You will get a message about how golems are going to kill you - fight them off when they become aggressive.
Repeat this process in the basement, where you will see Maeva stuck in a force field, and more attacking golems.
Once you have killed all of the golems, talk to Sieran who will tell you to find a dimensional anchor. The anchor is in the green circle, but it is up on the roof of the building. Go to the roof of the building, killing all the golems and turrets on the way. Alternatively, you can skip all the golems if you have enough health and quick moves.
There is a doorway on the roof blocked by a force field. Use the control panel next to the doorway to turn off the force field. Then go through the doorway and get attacked by more golems and turrets.
Turn left and go up the stairs. The Dimensional Anchor is sitting on the ground next to where a turret is. Skill 1 stuns and damages foes, while skill 2 launches them.
Go to the basement and use skill 2 - with Maeva free, the golems will become friendly and any that remain will fight for you. Free Maeva, and trigger the Undead Scout to attack. A number of golems will come downstairs to help you in the fight. The final cutscene triggers upon the death of the scout.

== Walkthrough ==
You meet up with Almorra Soulkeeper and several other Vigil soldiers. The beaches ahead are swarming with Risen, and it's your goal to eliminate them all. The soldiers will split off in three directions: one group to the left, one to the middle, one to the right. It's up to you to decide where you want to fight.
This mission is largely luck-based; you're gambling on not drawing the attention of too many Risen at once, so that your NPC allies can soak up the damage. The Vigil do a decent job of staying alive, and you can revive them if needed. However, there are a lot of foes, and additional ones will come from the water periodically. If an entire group gets overwhelmed, it's a problem, since then the Risen will accumulate on that side; reviving all the troops takes time, and it is difficult to take on that many enemies at once.
You should prioritize taking out Risen Abominations and Risen Plague Carriers as soon as possible. They deal devastating damage and quickly wipe out NPCs if left unattended. Alternatively you can stay behind and use the arrow carts to kill the Risen with minimal effort or danger.
After all the Risen have been defeated, the mission is over, and you get a choice of what to do for the next mission.

== Walkthrough ==
Go into the circle as instructed and you will become an Avatar of Balthazar and receive new weapon skills for the rest of the mission. Take a look at your skills before proceeding as you will soon be fighting undead on the beach. As the skills are blasts and not area effect, try not to get surrounded since the skills only affect foes in front of you. Note that you retain your belt, utility, and elite skills (F1-F5 and slots 6-10), and the allied NPCs can be used as a buffer.

Avatar of Balthazar skills

As you approach Thadeus Ghostrite (champion, temporarily invulnerable) numerous undead will swarm towards you. Dispatch them with your newly acquired skillset.
Undead Abominations will spawn after a while, and a few undead later the objectives will update and allow you to attack Thadeus Ghostrite, who is immune to damage from your allies but not from your Avatar.
A special note that if you are a Mesmer, put the utility Mirror Images on your skill bar. The two summoned clones will use your full 1-5 skillset from the avatar effect, and can rip apart the boss Wraith in seconds. Engineers may also choose to use their weapon or tool kits - given the sheer number of enemies that can spawn, the Flamethrower is particularly useful. Belt skills such as Bandage Self, Incendiary Ammo, and Grenade Barrage may also be used.
Due to losing access to the profession and weapon skills, revenants also lose access to their utility and healing skills. This makes this mission slightly more difficult for revenants.

The Origins of Madness: A Moment's Peace is a Living World story instance as part of The Origins of Madness release. To enter the instance, the character must participate in the fight with the Twisted Marionette. The instance is repeatable, however the map marker and the sparkling star will not be visible at the entrance after the first visit.


== Objectives ==
part of The Origins of Madness
 Speak with Scholar Ela Makkay.
 Optional: Catch up with Rox.
 Optional: Catch up with Braham, Logan and Taimi.
 Optional: Catch up with Marjory and Kasmeer.


== Walkthrough ==
This instance only consists of dialogues. Talk to Ela Makkay until she mentions Scarlet's lair. Participating in the rest of the instance is optional.

The Nightmare Ends is the fifth story step of Tower of Nightmares, the fourth episode of Living World Season 1.


== Objectives ==
Leave the area to plan your next move.
Read the letter from Kasmeer.
The Nightmare Ends
Return to the tower core.
Find out the state of the tower from Marjory.
Search the area for a clue to the core's defenses.
Find a way to clear the vines.
Search the hidden room for a way to remove the core's defenses.
Search the lab for components: x/4
Use the forge to create a shield disabler.
Return to the tower's core.
Administer the final injection of antitoxin.
Defend Kasmeer while she creates an emergency portal!
Time remaining: 2:00
Use the portal to escape!
Complete!


== Rewards ==
Pristine Toxic Spore Sample (3)
Thorny Seed Pouch (2)
Writ of Tyrian Mastery


== Walkthrough ==
Speak with Vigil Tactician Steelbreaker under the Pact Helicopter at Thunder Ridge Camp. You find yourself in the Heart of the Tower again, with Marjory Delaqua and Kasmeer Meade.

Main chamber
Listen to the dialogue, and then interact with the Disabled Injector to salvage a Vial of Leftover Antitoxin. Use this on the Vine Passage to the southeast to enter Scarlet's hidden room of puzzles.

Puzzle room

In this room you require four puzzle pieces, with one piece retrieved from each of the Molten alliance coolant box, the Aetherblade Inquest data terminal, the Watchknight and the Toxic Spore Pod. You start the puzzle phase by interacting with Scarlet's Forge.
If you wish, you can skip each puzzle by selecting a combat option, you will however have to fight a group of Scarlet themed enemies.

Solving all 4 puzzles correctly awards the Nightmare Euthanizer achievement, while selecting combat options for all 4 instead awards the Nightmare Terminator achievement.
Note that there is a bright pink recording disc behind the Storage Tanks for the Investigative Record 2 achievement.
 Molten Coolant Box
When examining the controls for shutting down power, three slider panels need to be set. The correct solution to yield the Molten Iron Scrap and solve the puzzle is to select the three symbols which make up the Molten Alliance: Flame, icicle and iron.

For the Nightmare Terminator achievement, select the combat option "Force an overload." instead.
 Inquest Terminal
Retrieve the Aetherblade Data from the Inquest Terminal. Do this by interpreting the data quantitatively sorted by effectiveness (per Marjory's hint).

For Nightmare Terminator, select the combat option "Turn off power to the console." instead.
 Watchknight
Revive the defeated Watchknight, and then interact with the Asuran Recorder, which unlocks phrases to use when talking to the Watchknight. Select the option "Nobody breaks my toys but me!" and then retrieve the Watchwork Core.

For the combat version for Nightmare Terminator, unlock and select "These Watchknights you're so proud of? Mine now." instead, which will turn the Watchnight into a Veteran Twisted Nightmare.
 Toxic Spore Pod
Pick up the Sturdy Stick and the Dry Roots. Combining the Sturdy Stick and the Dry Roots at the nearby Lab Table will allow you to soak the dry roots in lamp oil to receive Oil Soaked Roots. Interacting with the Fire Pot will directly provide you with a torch bundle. The torch can then be used to heat the Toxic Spore Pod, releasing the Dried Toxic Spore.

For Nightmare Terminator, select "Try to smash the pod open." instead.
 Scarlet's Forge
Once you have acquired all four pieces, interact with Scarlet's Forge again to create a Shield Disabler to remove the shield from the tower core in the first chamber.

Optionally if you want to unlock the other mutually exclusive achievement (Nightmare Terminator or Nightmare Euthanizer), you could log out here and return to the start of the instance.
Back in the main chamber
When you prompt her to do so, Marjory removes the shielding and administers the final dose of anti-toxin. Inevitably this triggers the appearance of some angry Toxic alliance foes, including a particularly tough champion, the Knight of Rot. You only need to fight this foe for a short time before Kasmeer finishes the emergency escape portal, at which point using the portal will complete and exit the instance.

For the Fight at the Finish achievement, ignore the time limit and Kasmeer's Portal, staying behind until you defeat the Knight of Rot.
A cinematic showing the destruction of the tower will play upon returning to Kessex Hills.


=== Achievements ===

Complete the mission.

Letter from Grand Duchess Faolain: Found in the southeast room on a crate.

Sitting at the base of the largest Storage Tank in the center of the hidden puzzle room.

Solve the four puzzles without using the combat option.

Use combat to complete all four puzzles:
for the Inquest Terminal select "Turn off power to the console."
for the Molten Coolant Box select "Force an overload."
for the Toxic Spore Pod select "Try to smash the pod open."
for the Watchknight puzzle, unlock and use the phrase "These Watchknights you're so proud of? Mine now."

Defeat the Knight of Rot before leaving the instance.
The Knight of Rot can take a lot of damage before dying and delivers a lot of damage in melee. Keep dodging and fight him at ranged or from his flanks or behind him in melee.
Hostile Toxic Alliance NPCs and Toxic Stalks spawn throughout the area during the Knight of Rot's fight. Be careful with your movement and positioning with the latter.
The timer running out does not cause you you to fail this achievement nor the objectives of the instance.
When the timer runs out, the game will warn you that you have 30 seconds left. However, nothing happens when this additional time runs out.
The Knight of Rot must be defeated after Marjory and Kasmeer run away from the tower.

=== Solving the puzzles ===
Each of the four puzzles can be either solved by fighting against a group of Scarlet's foes, or by solving the puzzle. To trigger the fight, each device offers an attack option, indicated by the swords.


==== Molten puzzle ====
When examining the controls for shutting down power, three slider panels need to be set. The correct solution to yield the Molten Iron Scrap and solve the puzzle is to select the three symbols which make up the Molten Alliance: Flame, icicle and iron.


==== Aetherblade puzzle ====
The task is to retrieve the Aetherblade Data from the Inquest Terminal. There are two ways to achieve this: The first is to interpret the data quantitatively sorted by effectiveness (matching Marjory's hint). The second option is to collate the data into qualitative results repeatedly until a new third option appears to bypass the console's interpretation protocols.


==== Watchknight puzzle ====
After reviving the watchknight, two objects become available: Scribbled Diagrams and Asuran Recorder. Checking the recorder unlocks phrases that can be used with the watchknight. The scribbled diagrams hint that the deactivation phrase is something which Scarlet did not say during the Closing Ceremony. All three phrases will eventually yield the Watchwork Core. The first phrase, "Nobody breaks my toys but me!", will put the watchknight into sleep mode (literally). The second phrase, "These watchknights you're so proud of? Mine now.", will turn the watchknight into a hostile Veteran Twisted Nightmare. And the third phrase, "Nothing wrong with you I can't fix forever.", will make the watchknight explode.


==== Toxic puzzle ====
To open the Toxic Spore Pod, different items need to be combined. Combining the Sturdy Stick and the Dry Roots will yield the Makeshift Torch Handle which can then be soaked in the lamp oil at the lab table to get the Makeshift Torch. Interacting with the Fire Pot will then give a Torch that can be picked up. The torch can then be used to gather the Dried Toxic Spore.

== My story ==

The Verdant Brink is the first major zone players enter in the Heart of Thorns expansion pack, and is the entrance to the Heart of Maguuma region. The aftermath of the Pact's disastrous assault on Mordremoth is most visible here, with massive vines and still-burning airship wreckage strewn across the landscape. The local Itzel hylek have made fast friends of the newcomers, and will accept Airship Parts for unique and valuable supplies.
To secure the area, pockets of Pact survivors and the Itzel tribe can be assisted in their survival against the Mordrem. In the daytime, each outpost needs help in gathering survivors and assembling defenses. During the night, the Mordrem attack in full force, creating a zone-wide battleground to hold rally points and recover supplies. Towards the end of the night, powerful Mordrem lieutenants take residence in the canopy of Verdant Brink, and must be brought down.


== Getting there ==
Complete the story step Prologue: Rally to Maguuma from the Heart of Thorns story once, which then unlocks account-wide access to the portal from the Silverwastes described below.
From the Silverwastes: the portal to Verdant Brink is in the south-western part of the map, through a door behind Amber Sandfall.
From Auric Basin: the portal to Verdant Brink is in the north-west corner of the map, near  Wanderer's Waypoint — .
From the Lost Precipice guild hall: the portal to Verdant Brink is in the southeastern corner of the map.

== Events ==

The majority of events in Verdant Brink are part of the two consecutive map-wide meta events based on the in-game Day and night cycle. Events during dusk will count towards the day events and during dawn – towards the night events. 
During daytime, the map meta-event is Securing Verdant Brink, which focuses on building up the five outposts through their respective event chains in order to prepare for the night. At night, the map meta event is Night and the Enemy, where players need to defend multiple rally points against waves of enemies and, in the later half of the night, fight the bosses in the canopy. Successful completion of events during the night increases the level of rewards in 4 tiers.

=== Night and the Enemy ===
During the night, events are at first focused on building up and defending rally points and then on slaying the bosses in the canopy during the second part of the night. There are up to four rally points per outpost, for a maximum of 20 in total. Maintaining control of rally points around an outpost during the three defense waves which occur during the first half of the night is critical for map meta-event progression. When under Pact control, each rally point has a supply level which can be filled by bringing Pact Supplies to the rally point and escorting soldiers. Raising the supply level of a rally point allows it to build extra defenses such as barricades and turrets, making the rally point easier to defend. Each Pact Supply that a player deposits increases the supply level by 1/5 of a tier and each escorted Pact soldier raises it by a full level. 
Once the Pact Choppers descend halfway through the night (20:30 left on the timer until daybreak), bosses appear in the canopy, one corresponding to each outpost. Along with defense of rally points, killing all the bosses is critical for progressing the map meta-event to tier 4 as these two event types contribute the most to increasing the night-time security level.
Thus, during the first half of the night, making sure rally points are defended during the Mordrem assaults (and retaking any which have been overrun by Mordrem) should be the main priority, followed by escorting soldiers, running supplies and killing rampaging Mordrem. When the bosses appear, slaying them should be a first priority. To achieve these goals, it is important that players spread out evenly across the map in small groups. To reach tier 4 night, about tier 2.5 needs to be achieved from the defense events and all the bosses need to be slain. Completing any Nighttime event will award the player one stack of  Pact Supplier. This increases experience gained from kills by up to 5%.

== Rewards ==
 Airship Parts are the zone's currency, awarded for completing events and opening Airship Cargo. These can be used to purchase pieces of Bladed armor, recipes needed to craft Minstrel gear, various collection trophies and more.
Pact Crowbars are awarded for each day-time event completed, and for each tier reached during the night-time meta event. These can be used to open Airship Cargo chests that are scattered throughout Verdant Brink. Cargo spawns will be indicated by red pings on the minimap.
Night-time rewards revolve around getting the map meta event completion to tier 4. This is done through completion of events and killing area bosses. Upon successfully reaching tier 4 night, the map meta event reward will have a chance of awarding a Bladed Armor Box. The chance increases with higher map participation, with it being a guaranteed award with 100% or above map participation.

== Walkthrough ==
The mission starts in an instance as soon as you enter the Desert Highlands. Talk to Shadows Agent Kito and after some conversation leave the outpost, jumping over the wall since they won't open the gate for you.
In the marked area, there are three optional objectives; destroy Forged catapults, kill three elite Forged groups, and (a hidden objective) help ten Nomads escape. Your main goal, though, is to reach the plateau to the northwest. Ascend it with your mounts and face the Herald of Balthazar once more. Get in her face and engage. Her attacks are, initially, a slowly rotating wall of flame and an AoE smash that are both easily avoided by getting behind her. As the fight progresses, the Herald will summon flame cages to imprison you and flaming explosions will appear all over the place. Dodge through or avoid the various hazards and you will eventually bring her down.
Ascend Godfall Tower and confront Balthazar himself. Whether or not you attack him, after a short time he overpowers you - but just as he's about to finish you off, you are saved by an unlikely ally. Talk to your friends, in either order, to finish the instance.
Back in the open world, start collecting the 12 crystal shards indicated on the map. To collect them all, you need to get the Springer mount, and in order to get to that, you need to unlock the third Raptor mount mastery, Canyon Jumping, to cross Highjump Gap or visit Lieutenant Zhao in End of Dragons. Then get to a spot where you can contact Taimi. After talking to her, if you've collected enough crystal shards, you will get the prompt to head for Glint's lair. Go east from Makali Outpost Waypoint and hop over the flaming gate with your Springer to complete the mission.


=== Achievements ===

Complete the instance.

The Flame Wall is similar to Sabetha's Firestorm attack: she will telegraph a thin orange cone on the ground before creating a fire wall that slowly rotates 360° anti-clockwise around the arena. Stand to the left of the orange cone (relative to standing on the cone while facing the Herald) to avoid having to outrun the wall; if you're unable to do this in time, get as close to the Herald as possible to make your escape easier.

This is a difficult achievement to solo. High DPS builds are recommended, as is teaming up with friends.
All members of the patrol group must be slain, not just the elite member.
The patrol groups will, true to their name, patrol the green circle on the map. They may wander outside the instance area, so be careful when following them that you don't get kicked from the instance.
Achievement qualification may be tracked via the  Qualify for Elite Elimination effect.
The timer won't begin counting down until the instance owner climbs the walls surrounding the perimeter of the starting area. This fact may be taken advantage of in a group by having additional members kill two of the three elites, then have the instance owner jump the wall to join in the kill for #3.

There are four stationary Forged Catapults found around the battlefield, in the corners of the available map (not on the plateau). Destroy all four to get the achievement.
Achievement qualification may be tracked via the  Qualify for Damage Control effect.

== My story ==

The Crystal Oasis is a zone in the Crystal Desert. It was once a desert but since the diversion of the Elon River into the Crystal Desert, the vegetation has grown and life in the oasis is now prosperous. The area is inhabited by elonians who have escaped the yoke of the Kingdom of Palawa Joko and have founded the Free City of Amnoon, as well as a Temple of Kormir. Several pyramids can be seen in the landscape, among them the Teratohedron, whose origin is unknown.

Complete the Story mission Sparking the Flame from Path of Fire (The ship will stay there after in Lion Arch near Phoenix Roost for later use).
The Lionguard Aircrew at Sanctum Harbor in Lion's Arch will take here any character who has already unlocked this zone through the storyline.
Use the Gem Store item Invitation to "Lily of the Elon".

== Trivia ==
"Crystal Oasis" is the name of a piece from the original Guild Wars soundtrack.

The Desert Highlands is a zone in the northern part of the Crystal Desert, although it is part of the desert, this area is more prosperous since it has more vegetation, so a tribe of ogres have settled in the northern part.
This zone contains the Palace of Aban which is guarded by the djinn, the Tomb of the Primeval Kings where the Primeval Kings are buried, and what was previously Glint's Lair, before the Elder Dragon Kralkatorrik defeated her in Prophet's Fall.


== Getting there ==
The Desert Highlands can be reached by using the Diviner's Gate, located to the north of Crystal Oasis. Following the road leading from Elona Reach to the Diviner's Passage leads to the gate. The gate is used during The Sacrifice story step, but it can be used to enter the map prior to starting the story.

== Walkthrough ==
The airship is docked next to the Phoenix Roost lighthouse in Lion's Arch. You can speak to the first mate before boarding for some extra dialogue.
Once the airship has landed, make your way down, reaching the entrance of a nearby tomb. Once you've entered the tomb, you will have to defeat the Forged inside; after they've been defeated, the Herald of Balthazar will appear. During this boss fight, she will often disengage in order to attack nearby civilians. After reaching around 80% HP, she will flee. Start following her.
The Herald will lead you to a nearby village that's also being attacked by Forged forces. Dispatch them and confront the Herald again. This time she will disappear, summoning two Forged Warhounds. Try to pull them one by one, dodge their flame projectiles and AoE or hide behind a small column near Aksim and Tasa. After you've defeated them, talk to Tasa and Aksim back at the start of the village. Aksim will task you with a renown heart: Use a raptor to save Seeker's Village. Use the Water Buckets and the Lionguard Fire Extinguisher to extinguish the nearby flames and use the newly-acquired raptor mount in order to reach and revive defeated Villagers. Once you've completed the renown heart, talk to Aksim again. This will unlock the raptor mount for use anytime, as well as unlock the Path of Fire masteries.
Head north into the mine and use your raptor to jump across gaps. Dispatch of the spiders infesting the mine in order to continue. Head further north until you reach the exit of the mine, talk to the nearby Miner and head south, towards the Free City of Amnoon. Once there, the nearby Cavalier will talk to you, finishing this story step.
If you stay in the instance after receiving the reward, you can talk to Kasmeer and Rytlock.


=== Achievements ===

No extra effort is required to complete this achievement, as you will be unlocking the raptor mount as part of the mission.

Achievement qualification may be tracked via the  Qualify for Fireproof Heart effect. This effect is removed if you take damage from the fires after starting this segment of the story.

Achievement qualification may be tracked via the  Qualify for Hammer and Tongs effect. This effect is removed if your character is struck by the Herald of Balthazar's charged-up hammer attack.

No effort is required to complete this achievement. You will automatically receive it as soon as the airship arrives in the Crystal Desert.

Complete the story mission.

liMaps.strWikiText:
Small Victory (Epilogue) is the thirteenth chapter and epilogue of the Path of Fire storyline.


== Objectives ==
Regroup in Amnoon.
Travel to Amnoon.
Enter the City.
Speak with Taimi.
Talk to the messenger.
Speak with Chief Councilor Imann.
Optional: Seek advice from your friends.
Optional: Check in with others around Amnoon.
Give your speech.
Regroup with your team at the docks.


== Rewards ==
Piece of Common Unidentified Gear (3)
Imann's Grateful Gift


== Walkthrough ==
Enter the instance near Amnoon Waypoint. Speak to Taimi, then join the party in your honor. You may speak to your friends and acquaintances before giving your grand victory speech. You'll have to choose in which tone to start the speech with, in which tone to continue and in which tone to end the speech - either upbeat, vague or somber.
Regroup with your team at the docks, discuss the challenges ahead and watch the fireworks. The reunion is cut short as Kralkatorrik takes flight once more, branding even more of Elona.


=== Achievements ===

Complete the instance.

Only the story instance owner is eligible for this achievement.
After Chief Councilor Imann asks you to take the stage whenever you're ready, /dance in front of the stage with the musicians on the south side of the room. Stand right up against the edge of the stage.
You will gain the  Dance Leader effect if you're standing in the right place.
This needs to be done BEFORE you give your speech, and before talking to any of the guests to trigger.

You don't actually need to speak with everyone, just people with an icon over their head: your companions and some NPCs you interacted with previously in the story.
Achievement qualification may be tracked via the  Social Butterfly effect. This will indicate how many people are left.

Speak to Deputy Qais to receive Lateen Sail

Speak to Wurmmarshal Osa Ekolo to receive Palawa's Personal Tapestry

Speak to Second Spear Nayrim to receive Embroidered Sunspear Sigil

The Desolation is a harsh landscape that is the central home for Palawa Joko and his forces. Once plentiful and luscious land, it had suffered cataclysmic changes centuries ago during the war between rebel god Abaddon and other gods. The Mouth of Torment now forever scars the place of the disastrous events, connecting Tyria with the Realm of Torment.
In the past two centuries since Joko has conquered Elona, the Elon River had been diverted, flooding the northern section of the Desolation, and The Bone Wall erected to mark the northern border of Joko's domain. The Bone Palace, the residence of the undead king, stands in the south.
The Desolation is an nigh-inhospitable place for mortals, which made it the ideal staging ground for Joko's invasion of Elona. For any Elonian seeking to defect north, the sulfurous sands and hordes of Awakened that patrol the land are lethal obstacles.


== History ==
Before the Exodus of the Gods, the lands that make up the Desolation were considered a lush and beautiful landscape, and was home to the Forgotten's empire. When Abaddon rebelled against the other Six Gods and laid siege to the Gates of Heaven, the war raged across the shores and islands of the Crystal Sea, and where Abaddon was struck down became a crater called the Ruptured Heart. Abaddon's defeat altered the landscape and created a tear in reality, connecting the land to the Realm of Torment that is the Mouth of Torment. From the Mouth of Torment, the influence of Abaddon and the Realm of Torment slowly seeped into the world, poisoning and warping the landscape into the sulfurous wasteland it is today.
In the decades following this, the Primeval Kings spread their reign further north, settling Vabbi and the Desolation, establishing the Dynastic Tombs and reaching further north into the Crystal Desert in 29 AE. They had also established Morah as a guard over the Mouth of Torment. However, due to Abaddon's spreading influence through the Mouth of Torment, Morah succumbed and fell nearly two hundred years later.
At some point, Sahlahja was established in the Desolation as well, being ruled by its own king during the Shattered Dynasty. It too eventually fell to the spread of the sulfurous haze as well as to Palawa Joko when he first attempted to conquer Elona. Since Joko's appearance and building of the Bone Palace, the only settlements that was able to be founded was Lannur, which Turai Ossa had established before moving his doomed Great Pilgrimage further north into the Crystal Desert. After this, the sulfurous sands became too deadly for mortals to cross into the land.
In 1075 AE, Abaddon's Margonite forces mustered in the Desolation and the landscape was transformed by countless tendrils that mimicked the hair of Abaddon's mask. After being freed, Palawa Joko assisted the Order of the Sunspears in crossing the Desolation in return for their help in reclaiming his throne and a number of his forces. With Abaddon's death that year, the sulfurous sands began to recede slowly, making the Desolation more hospitable over time. With Palawa Joko's second conquest of Elona, he had established new settlements in edges of the Desolation, the most prominent of which being Purity, which became one of Vabbi's largest source of farmed food. In the years of Joko's reign, the Order of Shadows splintered from the Order of Whispers and established the Chantry of Shadows overlooking both the Mouth of Torment and the Bone Palace.

The Elon Riverlands is a zone in the Crystal Desert. The place gets its name from the Elon River that runs through it.


== History and geography ==
Originally part of the Crystal Sea, it became a parched and arid land after the Exodus of the Gods for a millennia until Palawa Joko diverted the Elon River through the desert as part of his second invasion of Elona. The diverting of the Elon River has resulted in several pools of quicksand scattering the area, as well as a growth of verdant plantlife and migrating species, such as skimmers.
In the north lies Augury Rock and the Hall of Ascension within. Over the millennia several groups have attempted to reach Ascension, leaving various ruins scattering the area and its northern neighbor, the Crystal Oasis. Among the ruins are the remains of Turai Ossa's failed colony. Nowadays, pilgrims known as Followers of Ascension have gathered from across Central Tyria and Elona to research or attempt the ancient rite of Ascension.
To the south, along with the Elon River stands Joko's imposing Bone Wall, which marks the northern border of his kingdom. Those who have broken Joko's laws are exiled just beyond the Bone Wall, forced into labor camps to toil in fields under the oppression of Joko's Awakened who watch over the area from The Deadhouse.

== Walkthrough ==
Note that this mission begins immediately after Beast of War finishes - you may wish to exit the instance first and talk to Taimi at a Contact Point to avoid missing a progress point for the "Always Time for Taimi" achievement.
Once more, you face Balthazar in combat, this time wielding the god-made blade Sohothin.
As is to be expected, the god of war is a formidable opponent, using powerful AoE attacks and aided by endless hordes of Forged hounds. But you're not facing him alone: as soon as he loses 10% of his health, Aurene appears to assist you. She'll drop bright orbs that grant barrier and  Gift of the Scion; at other times she will envelop herself in a glowing sphere and offer to share her power with you. Stand inside the sphere to receive temporary invulnerability and  Dragon's Rage.
Most of Balthazar's attacks telegraph themselves clearly using orange markers on the floor; thus, most of his attacks can be avoided with good reflexes. He will perform a slam attack that sends out a fiery shockwave that knocks back; this can be jumped over to save endurance. Don't be afraid to switch back to your normal weapons (use weapon swap) if you find yourself struggling to avoid Balthazar's AoEs due to unfamiliarity with Sohothin; it will "sheathe" to your special action key, allowing you to take it out again any time you wish.
Balthazar will occasionally shield himself and begin to charge up his ultimate attack - the one that killed you last time. The only way to stop him is to coordinate with Aurene. Break her out of her chains, then run to the blue circle near Balthazar's shield and press your special action key to perform the Coordinated Attack (unlocked). At other times, Balthazar will shield himself using Dire Shield Generators; destroy these on sight.
Eventually, you'll deliver the final blow and witness the death of a god. You'll be dazed by the  Divine Fallout. Aurene flies off, leaving you to confer with your dazed friends, who agree to reconvene at Amnoon.


=== Achievements ===

Complete the instance.

Note that this achievement is only available to the instance owner and not to other party members.
Weapon swap to return to your normal skills; Sohothin will be "sheathed" to your special action key. As your joint attack with Aurene also uses the special action key, take care not to accidentally unsheathe it.
If you are downed or defeated, you will automatically re-equip Sohothin upon revival. So long as you do not hit Balthazar with any of Sohothin's skills you can "resheath" and still progress the achievement.
Hidden Achievement not shown in the Mastery panel for Act 3.
Achievement qualification may be tracked via the  Who Needs a Magic Sword effect. The achievement will be awarded during the cutscene if successful.

Note that this achievement is only available to the instance owner and not to other party members.
Balthazar uses his Ultimate Attack if you fail to perform the joint attack with Aurene in time.

== Walkthrough ==
The mission largely takes place in the open world. Talk to Captain Rahim and then to the three people he indicates (in any order):

Deputy Ayoub: Complete Priestess Karima's renown heart tasks: Bring food, water and medicine to the people who need it, and open shaking tents to discover and kill random monsters. Then talk to refugees until you have the information you need.
Deputy Qais: Go meet with casino owner Zalambur in his office, entering an instance. As you discuss your business, Palawa Joko's envoy Archon Iberu arrives with an offer Zalambur isn't meant to refuse. Kill the intruding Awakened, but you can ignore Iberu who is invulnerable and does not attack.
Chief Councilor Imann: In the conversation, decide whether Amnoon allies with Palawa Joko, the Sunspears, or stays neutral. The choices will impact ambient dialogue in Amnoon, the banners you see in Amnoon, and the NPCs that appear (in Path of Fire and Season 4). It will also impact some later mission rewards and collections unlocked (Raise the Banners: Amnoon Independence, Raise the Banners: Salute to Palawa Joko, or Raise the Banners: Sunspear Support).
Move to one of the indicated high points on the map (marked with a radio signal icon) to contact Taimi, read your mail, and return to Zalambur. Talk to him and then to your guildmates to end the mission.

== Walkthrough ==
The first part of the mission takes place in the open world. Talk to the two cavaliers indicated on the map. They will each direct you to a Forged camp near them.
In the northern camp, all you have to do is to destroy enough of the respawning cannons. You can use the Forged Ammunition lying around to speed this up, as they can destroy the cannons in one hit.
In the eastern camp, you have to find three pieces of intelligence among many false leads. Running up to a lead will cause you to say something, and the right targets will be highlighted with a green star when you get close to them. There are four possible items that can be found, but only three are needed.

A cart full of branded rocks in the central area.
A Forged scrap on top of a crate.
A metal plate inside a small building.
A Forged Husk on the western tower.
After completing both camps, move east and enter the story instance where Rytlock and Canach join you. Kill the two guards at the gate, then move through the camp to the indicated target. When you get close to a sentry (marked with an eye symbol), they'll run off toward a Forged brazier to call for reinforcements. Throwing some Forged explosives at them is a good way to stop them dead in their tracks, as it were, as well as cripple and chilled. Everyone else you can kill at your leisure.
After you dispatch the guards at the second and third gate, you're tasked with killing the four marked Veteran Forged Officers. There are again three sentries (also marked on your map) and a lot of Forged to be wary of. If you're having trouble, stay back and pull them towards you at the gate to take them out individually. There's no time limit, so take your time and clear them as quick or slow as needed.
As soon as the officers are dead, a Forged Bastion appears at the center, and any remaining Forged (including sentries) run away. This boss is very resilient (self-applies Protection), has devastating (if slow) ranged attacks, and summons reinforcements. Remove his Protection boon to take him down faster. After he's lost about two thirds of his health, he'll retreat to the central brazier and make a stand there. During this phase, he will also occasionally rotate a complete circle firing groups of projectiles.
After beating the Bastion, move northwest to the Temple of Kormir and speak with people there. After a bit of conversation, the Herald of Balthazar will appear and attack you again. After you've hurt her a bit (approximately down to 80%), she moves and starts attacking refugees. Use your Special action skill,   Move!, to call nearby refugees to your location and out of the way of her Herald's Doom attacks. After she's down to 25% health, she unleashes a final attack on the center of the temple, killing several priests (these do not count against the Shield of Kormir achievement), then flees into her portal again. Revive the fallen priests of Kormir to complete the mission.
Although technically not part of the story step, Taimi can also be contacted during it at any of the Contact Points for additional dialogue.


=== Achievements ===

Complete the story step.

Kill all officers and trash mobs in the instanced Forge. Once all officers are dead, the other forged will run away, so it's best to leave one officer alive until you've killed all other foes. When the Forged Bastion comes to the central area, you can ignore him and kill remaining foes. Come back and kill him when you're ready to leave the instance.
Achievement qualification may be tracked via the  Qualify for Leave None Alive effect.

Achievement qualification may be tracked via the  Qualify for Lurking among the Flames effect. This effect is removed if you fail to stop a sentry.

At specific intervals during the fight, beginning at 80%, the Herald of Balthazar will move to one of the groups of refugees in the temple and begin a Herald's Doom attack, killing all of them.
Use the   Move! special action skill to lure civilians to your location. It is a shout skill and will lure any refugee in range to your location (at the time you used the skill), meaning all 20 can be moved at once if they're all in range. If you stand a little behind the Herald while she's winding up her Herald's Doom attack and use the skill, the refugees will move to your location behind her. You can then continue to use it to pull them even further away. Since it's a shout, it has a good range, and there's enough time between her attacks to practice and see how far you can reach.
Giving them  Swiftness will help them leave the dangerous areas faster, and it is possible to prevent instant death from the hammer attack with  Aegis, but if they remain in the fire they will quickly die from burning.
As this chapter saves checkpoints at each stage, it is possible to relog after failing, and restart from the Temple of Kormir without having to replay the whole chapter.
The safest method is going ahead before the Herald ever reaches refugees as she will follow a fixed pattern. When she moves to the first group (which also grants you the skill), follow her and stand behind her at the first group. Use the Move! special action skill while she's winding up to pull the first group of refugees behind her, then keep spamming it while running around the temple to keep all of them following you. All refugees in range will follow you even if they do not have the Shield icons over their heads, and so it's possible to run to each group and gather all 20 of them (there's 5 groups of 4, which the Herald will attack in a counter-clockwise order), and lead them to a spot nowhere near the fight (such as the ramp you came in on) and comfortably fight the Herald for the remainder of the mission without worry. The Herald will be more likely to stick near the spot of her last attack fighting your NPC allies, so this is possible to do solo fairly easily.
Doing this with a friend can make it easier, as they can focus on damaging the Herald, while you focus on saving the civilians.
Achievement qualification may be tracked via the  Qualify for Shield of Kormir effect.

Read all six Strange Burning Scrolls in the Forged war camp. Refer to the Strange Burning Scroll page for a detailed guide.

== Walkthrough ==
Move south to enter the story instance at the indicated spot near Joko's Domain Waypoint. You'll shortly meet Archon Iberu. This boss will summon Awakened, create crippling tar AoEs, charge at you and drain lifeforce from his minions which restores a huge portion of his health. To interrupt Iberu's drain skill and momentarily stun him, attack and kill the single Awakened target he is draining. This target will be indicated by a circle over them while they are being drained, but it will be very hard to tell which is the target if the mobs are bunched together.  Try to keep the minions spread out enough during the fight to tell them apart.  
Now Kasmeer will make you and your group appear to be Iberu and his minions, providing you the  Lyssa's Guise disguise effect and a different  Lyssa's Guise to the team. Follow the indicated path to the palace. The palace guard will briefly attack you but then recognize you as Iberu. Go meet Grand Vizier Utumishi and Wurmmarshal Osa Ekolo, then leave the palace again to talk to your team.

Seek the aid of Troopmarshal Olori Ogun
Back in the open world, travel to the Domain of Vabbi where the Forged and the Awakened are at war. Go meet your next "colleague", Troopmarshal Olori Ogun, in another instance.
Your task now is to attack the Forged with a bunch of Ogun's freshly dead recruits. You get a set of new skills to do this:

Mummy Army skills

Party members will transform into awakened mummy's and get those skills

Party members also gain a pulsing Stability effect.
"Melee Attack" (1) orders your force to attack an enemy, "Ranged Attack" (2) does the same thing at range, "Mummy Decoy" (3) makes one of your mummies attract enemy attention (and then blow themselves up on your command), and "Come to Me" (5) will rally nearby mummies to you. You can also switch back to your own skills with the special action key and enter combat yourself but your party members remain transformed for the rest of the mission.
Use (5) on the four Awakened Recruits nearby and lead them to glory. You can test out your army on the Forged Prowlers underway, but note that your soldiers' health does not regenerate, so avoiding combat is preferable.
Lead your troops to the nearby Forged Gate, kill the defenders and recruit two more mummies. The Hothead Forged Soldiers you encounter beyond the gate are immune to melee hits and need to be attacked at range (2). Inside the forge, the shielded Forged are only vulnerable after their shield generator is destroyed.
Assault the portal on the upper level of the facility, recruiting new troops as you proceed. Path to portal is from main hall, stairs on right leading down, follow path then stairs on left going up to platform with a room of four awakened troops. Down the stairs leads to portal. If your troop dies, you can recruit the four in room. First take out the shielded soldier near the portal by dodging through the flame walls behind him and destroying the shield generator. The Elite Foundry Overseer guarding the portal switches between immunity to melee and immunity to ranged, so pay attention to his status when targeting him. Destroy the portal and return to Ogun, then talk to your team.

Seek the aid of Beastmarshal Oluwa Eranko
After leaving the instance, travel south to the Necropolis to meet Beastmarshal Oluwa Eranko in another instance. Again you need to prove your skills as a necromancer. Eranko teaches you "Joko's Grasp", an ability that drains speed from enemies while mounted.
Mount your raptor and accept Eranko's challenge. Your task is to catch up with the Beast of the Valley and tag it at least thrice with Joko's Grasp:

Cycle through wayside enemies with "Tab" to drain speed from them to catch up.
Set the Beast as your target (Ctrl-T), then press T to return focus to it quickly.
Special action skill

Companion skills
Party members become Elonian ghosts with the incredible speed.

Then return to the starting point in the southwestern part of the circuit, accept the allegiance of the easily impressed Eranko, and talk to your team to complete the mission.

== My story ==

The Domain of Vabbi is a zone in Vabbi in the Crystal Desert. It features many locations from Guild Wars Nightfall, including Kodash Bazaar and the Garden of Seborhin.
Vabbi is a land of great wealth and lavish palaces. Under the rule of Palawa Joko, Vabbian culture has been subverted through centuries of propaganda, turning it into little more than an efficient machine for producing loyal Awakened. Most Vabbians now worship Joko as a god-king, eagerly serving him in both life and death.
The recent arrival of the Elder Dragon Kralkatorrik has ravaged much of the eastern side of the region, and the Brandstorm rages especially fiercely there. Balthazar's Forged have set up a staging ground for the assault on Vabbi in their relentless pursuit of the Elder Dragon.
